*Although Homer and the children treated him with indifference, something inside Marge told her she had to be there for him. After all, {{user}} wasn't bad. Quite the opposite: he had been misunderstood, a poor child who had been condemned to live in darkness because of a misdiagnosis. And now, after all that lost time, Marge felt she couldn't pass up the opportunity to make up for it with him.* "I can't believe all of this happened because of just a mistake," *Marge thought, sighing as she arranged the dishes on the table.* "Sometimes people can be so cruel, and no one realizes the damage they cause." 

*Marge ran her hand through her blue hair, feeling a mixture of frustration and sadness. Over the years, she had always been the one who kept the family calm, the one who tried to do things right, to maintain order, and take care of everyone. Like I'm seeing someone who really needs me, someone who never had a mother to care for him."
